record.context_brief: Strong unique continuation for p-harmonic functions.
record.original_question: Let 1 < p < infinity, let Omega be a connected open subset of R^n with n >= 2, and let u be a weak solution of the p-Laplace equation div(|grad u|^(p-2) grad u) = 0 in Omega. If u vanishes of infinite order at an interior point x_0 of Omega, must u vanish identically on all of Omega?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.2 (Strong unique continuation). Suppose u solves (1.1) and vanishes of infinite order at an interior point x0 of Ω, does u ≡ 0 on all of Ω?
Thus the problem, in both formulations 1.1 and 1.2, remains open in the case n ≥ 3, p != 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $1 < p < \infty$ and let $n \geq 2$. Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a connected open set, and let $u \in W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ be a weak solution of the $p$-Laplace equation
$$\operatorname{div}\bigl(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u\bigr) = 0 \quad \text{in } \Omega,$$
i.e., $\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u\cdot\nabla\varphi\, dx = 0$ for every $\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$. We say that $u$ vanishes of infinite order at an interior point $x_0 \in \Omega$ if for every integer $N \geq 1$,
$$\lim_{r \to 0^+} r^{-N} \int_{B_r(x_0)} |u|^p\, dx = 0,$$
where $B_r(x_0) \subset \Omega$ is the Euclidean ball of radius $r$ centered at $x_0$.

Question: If $u$ vanishes of infinite order at some interior point $x_0 \in \Omega$, must $u \equiv 0$ on all of $\Omega$?
artifact.category_tag: strong unique continuation for p-Laplace equation
artifact.status_search_result: The strong unique continuation property for weak solutions of the p-Laplace equation is known in the plane (n=2) and in the linear case p=2 (classical Aronszajn-type results). For n≥3 and p≠2 the problem remains open; surveys and recent works on unique continuation for the p-Laplacian (e.g., partial results via Almgren-type frequency functions, including on the Heisenberg group under boundedness assumptions) continue to treat it as an open question.

status_evidence.title: On the problem of unique continuation for the p-Laplace equation
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses unique continuation for the p-Laplace equation and notes that the strong unique continuation property remains open for n≥3 when p≠2.
status_evidence.claim: The strong unique continuation problem for p-harmonic functions is open in dimensions n≥3 with p≠2.

status_evidence.title: The unique continuation property of p-harmonic functions on the Heisenberg group
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes partial unique continuation results for p-harmonic functions under a frequency-boundedness assumption, indicating the general problem is unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Only conditional/partial results are available beyond the cases n=2 or p=2.
